[GOOS:windows] skip 'logos conc needs named pipes'
[GOOS:plan9] skip 'logos conc needs named pipes'

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# One thread only: the fault is the order the spawns give, and stealing
# the second child onto another thread would hide it.
env GOMAXPROCS=1

cd shake

# The linter and the race detector accept the order the spawns give:
# the channel carries the order, and no memory is raced.
logos lint ./...
! stderr .
[race] [cgo] env CGO_ENABLED=1
# Under -race the runnext slot is randomized and the spawn order does
# not hold, so this step checks only that both children ran with no race.
[race] [cgo] logos test -race -count=1 -run TestBothRan ./ord
[race] [cgo] stdout '^ok '

# Without a shake the child the group started last runs first and takes
# the lock twice before the other child sends, so the order holds.
logos conc test -count=1 ./ord
stdout '^ok '
! stderr .
logos conc run ./ord
stdout '^locked,direct$'
! stderr .

# With shake seed 1 the lock taker yields at its start and at each
# acquire, so the direct child sends first and the test fails. The
# command prints the seed that replays the schedule.
! logos conc test -shake=1 -count=1 ./ord
stdout 'order = '
stderr 'shake seed 1'
! logos conc test -shake=1 -count=1 ./ord
stdout 'order = '
stderr 'shake seed 1'

# The same schedule fault shows in run: the program prints the flipped
# order and exits 2.
! logos conc run -shake=1 ./ord
stdout '^direct,locked$'
stderr 'shake seed 1'

# Without a value the seed comes from the clock and is printed, so the
# run can be replayed with -shake=<n>. A clock seed need not flip the
# order, so this step asserts only the seed line, not the exit status.
? logos conc test -shake -count=1 ./ord
stderr 'shake seed [0-9]+'

# A seed that is not a number is a usage error.
! logos conc test -shake=nope -count=1 ./ord
stderr 'is not a seed'

-- shake/go.mod --
module example.com/shake

go 1.27
-- shake/ord/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"logos/sync"
)

type box struct{ n int }

var gate sync.Locked[box]

func locked(first chan string) error {
	gate.WithLock(b => {
		b.n++
	})
	gate.WithLock(b => {
		b.n++
	})
	select {
	case first <- "locked":
	default:
	}
	return nil
}

func direct(first chan string) error {
	select {
	case first <- "direct":
	default:
	}
	return nil
}

func order(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	first := make(chan string, 2)
	go group (ctx) {
		go direct(first)
		go locked(first)
	}
	a := <-first
	b := <-first
	return a + "," + b, nil
}

func main() {
	got, err := order(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
		return
	}
	fmt.Println(got)
	if got != "locked,direct" {
		os.Exit(2)
	}
}
-- shake/ord/main_test.lgo --
package main

import "testing"

func TestOrder(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := order(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
		return
	}
	if got != "locked,direct" {
		t.Fatalf("order = %q, want %q", got, "locked,direct")
	}
}

func TestBothRan(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := order(t.Context())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
		return
	}
	if got != "locked,direct" && got != "direct,locked" {
		t.Fatalf("order = %q, want both children to send", got)
	}
}
